hints: Remember that not all viruses are the same, some store their genes as DNA and others store their genes as RNA, so what must be true for both types?
Think about which sugar and which bases are unique to DNA only or RNA only, and which base is shared by both types of nucleic acid.
walkthrough:
**Compare the three groups**

Prokaryotes and eukaryotes are cells, so they both contain DNA and RNA. Viruses are different because each virus has only one type of nucleic acid, either DNA or RNA, never both at once.

**Sort the sugars and bases**

Ribose sugar and uracil are found in RNA only. Deoxyribose sugar and thymine are found in DNA only. So none of these can be in every virus.

Shared rule to remember:
DNA bases = A, T, C, G and RNA bases = A, U, C, G

**Find what is always present**

Cytosine (C) is a base used in both DNA and RNA. Since every virus, prokaryote and eukaryote must have at least one type of nucleic acid, cytosine will always be present.

options.A: Ribose is the pentose sugar of RNA only, so DNA viruses have no ribose.
options.B: Deoxyribose is the pentose sugar of DNA only, so RNA viruses have no deoxyribose.
options.C: Cytosine is found in both DNA and RNA, so DNA viruses, RNA viruses, prokaryotes and eukaryotes all contain it.
options.D: Thymine is a DNA base only (replaced by uracil in RNA), so RNA viruses have no thymine.
